entities.summary:
Sostratus of Cnidus was a Greek architect and engineer who designed the lighthouse of Alexandria, one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World, on the island of Pharos off Alexandria, Egypt, in the 3rd century BCE. This claim is disputed among historians.

Sostratus was born in the 4th century BCE, but the exact date of his birth is unknown. He was a prolific architect who worked on various projects, including the construction of the Temple of Hephaestus in Athens, Greece. His designs were known for their innovative use of technology and engineering techniques.

Sostratus's legacy extends beyond his architectural works. He was a prominent figure in the Hellenistic period, during which the ancient Greek world was in a state of significant cultural, political, and economic transformation. His contributions to the field of engineering and architecture helped shape the course of Western civilization.

The lighthouse of Alexandria, which Sostratus designed, was a marvel of its time and a testament to the ingenuity of ancient Greek engineers. Despite its significance, the lighthouse has been the subject of much debate among historians, with some questioning its actual existence or the extent of Sostratus's involvement in its construction.
